previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 20%), COPD, type 2 diabetes, schizophrenia, and substance use was admitted for acute decompensated heart failure following a recent reduction in his torsemide dose from 40 mg to 20 mg. He presented with worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and leg swelling. Evaluation revealed pulmonary edema on chest imaging and elevated proBNP. He was treated with IV furosemide, which improved his symptoms and resolved his hypoxia and edema. His kidney function showed mild acute injury, likely due to over-diuresis, with creatinine rising to 1.4. He was stabilized at his dry weight of 88 kg, transitioned back to oral torsemide 20 mg daily, and had lisinopril reduced to 2.5 mg daily. He denied recent cocaine use, and urine toxicology was negative. He was discharged home with instructions to monitor daily weights, follow a low-sodium diet, and attend follow-up with a heart failure specialist, with outpatient lab monitoring planned.

Brief Hospital Course:
#) GASTROENTERITIS: Admitted for diarrhea and fever.  No 
leukocytosis.  Was in setting of raw chicken ingestion.  Stool 
studies sent and started on ceftriaxone monotherapy.  Clinically 
worsened and spiked a fever again and triggered for tachycardia 
to the 130s on ___, so broadened therapy empirically to 
vancomycin, cefepime, metronidazole and received several boluses 
of 500cc normal saline to support systolic blood pressures.  All 
stool studies, including c. diff, campylobacter, salmonella, ova 
+ parasties have come back negative.  Was concern for occult 
abscess, so CT torso obtained which was unremarkable with regard 
to an explanation for his symptoms.  Likely viral 
gastroenteritis vs. bacterial preformed toxin which resulted in 
decompensated heart failure with fluid resuscitation.

#) acute on chronic systolic heart failure: According to heart 
failure clinic notes, euvolemic weight is 89 kg, but peaked here 
to 94 kg with volume resuscitation in setting of hypotension.  
Resuscitation supported pressures but likely impaired forward 
flow resulting in transient elevated transaminases and acute 
kidney injury.  Each sequela resolved with cautious diuresis.  
Back at euvolemic weight (88.4 kg) on discharge.  Patient 
discharged on previous regimen of lisinopril 2.5 mg daily, 
torsemide 20 mg daily.

#) ELEVATED TRANSAMINASES: Likely secondary to heart failure 
exacerbation.  Ischemic upon congestive injury in the setting of 
decompensated heart failure with transient hypotension.  
Hepatocellular injury pattern resolved with diuresis.  No signs 
of liver failure.  Does have hepatitis C.  

#) PNEUMONIA: Fever, cough, fever, radiographic characteristics 
on CT consistent with infiltrate and new oxygen requirement.  
Likely superimposed pulmonary edema.  Improved on PO 
levofloxacin x 5 days.  Course of antibiotics completed ___. 
 Monitored QT in setting of quinolone use concurrent with 
ondansetron.  Titrated off of supplemental oxygen without 
difficulty.

#) ___ on CKD: Cr 1.6 on admission in the setting of acute 
illness and volume overload with good urine output.  Improved 
with diureses - thought to be secondary to impaired forward 
flow/congestion in the setting of decompensated heart failure.  
Trended back to baseline of 1.1-1.2 upon discharge.
